title: Gas Pains
summary:
Gas Pains
Gasoline prices continue to climb despite ample supplies and adequate domestic stockpiles. The apparent disconnect leaves the public and industry members scratching their pocketbooks. Last week's Tanker Opinion discussed the rising trend of product exports from domestic refineries and its implications for the clean product tanker markets.

children.title: Questioning the Economics
children.summary: The chart below shows US refinery utilization over the last year as well as the relative activity of PADD 1, PADD 2, and PADD 3 refiners. As discussed last week and in previous opinions, the price divergence between WTI and Brent crude oil benchmark contracts is creating a very favorable margin environment for PADD 2 refiners with access to the more cheaply‐priced WTI benchmark‐related crude oils and is evidenced through higher utilization figures.

children.title: Spelling Relief
children.summary: The question of high domestic pricing remains in spite of this set of extraordinary circumstances that would seemingly result in negative price movements or a better reconciliation of supply imbalances within the domestic US market. Expect the quality and price arbitrage to continue to pull product out of PADD III and sustain or even increase the need for incremental imports on the East Coast.
